question: Due to which of the following events did Rabindranath Tagore return the title of 'Knighthood' to the British Government while expressing his anguish?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Jallianwala Bagh massacre.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​​​​​​The **Amritsar Massacre,** also known as the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, happened on** April 13, 1919**. At the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab, a sizable peaceful crowd had gathered to protest the** Rowlatt Act and the detention of pro-independence activists Saifuddin Kitchlew and Satyapal. **
 
• In opposition to the mass murder in **Jalianwalla Bagh**,** Tagore surrendered his knighthood**. Rabindranath Tagore's letter to Lord **Chelmsford**, the British viceroy, in which he revoked his knighthood in opposition to the mass murder at** Jalianwalla Bagh.**
 
• The **Nobel laureate** was given a moving account of the slaughter by** Ruchi Ram Sahni,** a former Trustee of The Tribune, which led Tagore to decline the** knighthood. In 1915, **two years after winning the Nobel Prize for Literature,** Rabindranath Tagore was made a knight.**
 
• The term** "knight" **might be applied to positions of **higher aristocracy**, such as landowners, despite the fact that it was mainly a title for a **military function**. In exchange for the vassals' fidelity, defence, and service, the higher nobles grant them their fiefs, or parcels of land. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​​​On 14 January 1931, on the day of Makar Sankranti, the British military force surrounded and open gunfires on the public present in the peaceful public meeting of freedom fighters at Singhpur **Charanpaduka Maidan** located on the banks of Urmila river in Chhatarpur district Madhya Pradesh. Charan Paduka Massacre has been called as the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre of Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The Partition of Bengal was announced on **19 July 1905** by the then **Viceroy Lord Curzon**. It was implemented on **16 October 1905**. However, in 1911 it was **withdrawn **by **Lord Hardinge**. The stated reason was to ease the administration. But the actual reason was to weaken the growing nationalism in Bengal and break the unity.
 
• The **Chauri Chaura incident took place in British India **on** February 4, 1922, at Chauri Chaura** in the Gorakhpur district of the United Province (modern Uttar Pradesh),** when a sizable crowd of demonstrators** taking part in the Non-cooperation movement battled with police, who then opened fire.
